items.exactPrompt: Use case: photorealistic-natural. Create ONE original professional editorial food photograph, landscape 3:2, showing a technologically CORRECT OPEN URAMAKI preparation stage BEFORE rolling and AFTER the rice-covered nori has been flipped. On a clean pale neutral stone work surface lies a thin half-sheet rectangular dark nori sheet, flat and fully visible, approximately 18 by 10 cm. The cooked short-grain sushi rice layer is UNDERNEATH the nori, touching the surface; the Nori is facing UP. Thin irregular white rice grains peek out along the near and far long edges, enough to show that rice is beneath, NOT a slab and NOT a white layer covering the nori top. Across the center of the exposed dark nori, parallel to the long edge, lies ONE neatly squeezed narrow soft off-white cream-cheese road about 1 cm wide with natural slight piping ridges, and exactly THREE slender crisp cucumber batons running along the same road. The batons are long narrow green-skinned pale-green firm flesh, modest natural variation, no large seed core. Filling is restrained and low, not a huge frosting mound. Most of the dark slightly wrinkled matte nori top is visible around this central filling. The entire sheet remains OPEN FLAT and unrolled. There is NO fish and NO shrimp anywhere. Camera approximately 45 degrees from above, close but the complete rectangular assembly is visible with safe margins. Match the existing neutral food-card photographs: soft neutral side daylight, quiet light background, believable fine rice grains, slightly rippled nori texture, real fresh cucumber and soft cheese detail, gentle contact shadows and restrained sheen. Do not make rice ABOVE the nori in this filling stage; correct reverse-roll orientation is nori top, rice underside. No plate, mat, film, tool, piping bag, hands, people, extra ingredients, salmon, sesame, sauces, garnish, text, logo, flags, watermark, packaging, UI, game screenshot, frame, cartoon, CGI, plastic look, perfect cloned grains, floating food or impossible geometry. This is an original photographic process reference, not a finished 3D model or reward screen. Do not copy a source photograph.
